scope: Empire State Building, New York City
title: Empire State Building
blurb: The 102 story Art Deco skyscraper at 350 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, the world's tallest building from 1931 to 1970. This detailed model breaks the tower into seven setback stages, from the five story limestone base to the dirigible mooring mast, with the Art Deco lobby, the three observatories, and the 73 elevator banks inside.

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: Concrete footings, mat, and bedrock anchors below street level, carrying the 365,000 short ton weight of the building.

systems.name: Base
systems.description: The five story Indiana limestone base filling the whole city block, with the Fifth Avenue entrance, the side entrances, and the storefronts.

systems.name: Lobby
systems.description: The three story Art Deco lobby interior, with marble, terrazzo, bronze motifs, and the building relief.

systems.name: Shaft
systems.description: The 81 story setback shaft between the base and the crown, in seven stages with limestone piers, recessed window bays, and aluminum spandrels.

systems.name: Setback terraces
systems.description: Open terraces at each setback level, stepping the tower back as required by the 1916 Zoning Resolution.

systems.name: Steel frame
systems.description: The riveted steel frame and the central utility core, revealed when the model is exploded.

systems.name: Elevators
systems.description: The 73 elevators in vertical banks in the central core, with express shuttles to the observatories.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The 16 story, 200 ft metal crown above the 86th floor, mostly mechanical, topped by the 102nd floor roof.

systems.name: Observatories
systems.description: The 80th, 86th, and 102nd floor observatories, visited by about four million tourists a year.

systems.name: Mast
systems.description: The mooring mast and pinnacle above the 102nd floor, first planned for docking dirigibles and now carrying broadcast antennas.

systems.name: Crown lighting
systems.description: Architectural lighting for the crown and mast, from the 1932 searchlights to the 1,200 LED fixtures of 2012.

explanations.spread footing grid: Concrete spread footings carry the 365,000 short ton weight of the building down to the rock. Their depth and spread are schematic.
explanations.bedrock mat slab: A concrete mat ties the footings together above Manhattan bedrock. Shown schematically below street level.
explanations.bedrock caisson anchors: Caisson anchors pin the mat to bedrock against wind uplift. Count and placement are schematic.
explanations.basement perimeter walls: Perimeter basement walls retain the earth around the below grade floors. Depth shown schematically.
explanations.five story base mass: The five story base occupies the entire lot, with the 81 story shaft set back sharply above it. It is clad in Indiana limestone panels that give the building its signature blonde color.
explanations.east base facade: The Fifth Avenue face of the base: black granite storefronts at ground level, alternating piers and window strips above, and a stone sill topping the fifth story.
explanations.west base facade: The rear face of the base, with the same limestone pier rhythm and storefront band as the other faces. Rhythm schematic.
explanations.north base facade: The 34th Street face of the base, carrying two of the side entrances with their stainless steel canopies.
explanations.south base facade: The 33rd Street face of the base, carrying two of the side entrances with their stainless steel canopies.
explanations.fifth avenue entry portico: The main entrance at the center of the Fifth Avenue elevation: three sets of metal doors flanked by molded piers.
explanations.triple height transom glazing: A triple height transom window with geometric patterns sits above the main entrance.
explanations.golden empire state lettering: Golden letters spelling Empire State sit above the fifth floor windows.
explanations.concrete entry eagles: A pair of sculpted concrete eagles crowns the molded piers that flank the Fifth Avenue entrance.
explanations.ground floor storefront band: First floor storefronts with aluminum framed doors and windows set in black granite ring the base.
explanations.west 33rd street entry: One of two entrances on 33rd Street, with a modernistic stainless steel canopy and triple windows above. Less elaborate than the Fifth Avenue entrance.
explanations.east 33rd street entry: One of two entrances on 33rd Street, with a modernistic stainless steel canopy and triple windows above.
explanations.west 34th street entry: One of two entrances on 34th Street, with a modernistic stainless steel canopy and triple windows above.
explanations.east 34th street entry: One of two entrances on 34th Street, with a modernistic stainless steel canopy and triple windows above.
explanations.lobby interior volume: The three story lobby is the only space in the building with narrative motifs. Its shell is shown here; finishes are separate parts.
explanations.zigzag terrazzo floor: A zigzag terrazzo floor runs east to west through the lobby. Pattern shown schematically.
explanations.dark marble wainscot: Two tiers of marble line the lobby walls: darker wainscoting below, lighter stone above.
explanations.light marble upper walls: Lighter marble rises above the dark wainscoting to the coffered ceiling.
explanations.bronze narrative motifs: Bronze motifs of Electricity, Masonry, and Heating decorate the lobby walls.
explanations.lobby coffered ceiling: A coffered ceiling caps the three story lobby volume. Detail schematic.
explanations.west end escalators: Escalators at the west ends of the lobby rise to a mezzanine.
explanations.lobby mezzanine: A mezzanine overlooks the lobby from the west end, reached by the escalators.
explanations.information desk and anemometer: The information desk in the lobby; the 2009 renovation replaced its clock with an anemometer.
explanations.aluminum building relief: An aluminum relief of the building as built, without the antenna, stands at the west end of the lobby.
explanations.low rise column grid: Riveted steel columns rise through the base and lower tower. The building has 210 structural columns per floor; the grid shown is schematic.
explanations.mid rise column grid: The column grid narrows with the setbacks through the middle of the tower. Schematic.
explanations.high rise column grid: A tighter column grid carries the upper tower and crown. Schematic.
explanations.crown column grid: Steel columns inside the mechanical crown carry the mooring mast above. Schematic.
explanations.setback girder rings: Girder rings at the setback levels transfer the tower loads inward at each step. The setback floors are sourced; the rings are schematic.
explanations.central utility core: A central core carries elevators, stairs, and utilities the full height of the building. Interior space is at most 28 ft (8.5 m) deep from the core to the windows.
explanations.transfer girders at base: Deep transfer girders spread the tower columns across the five story base. Schematic.
explanations.floor diaphragm plates: Representative floor plates brace the frame at intervals up the tower. Schematic.
explanations.express elevator bank: Four express elevators built by Otis connect the lobby, the 80th floor, and landings in between.
explanations.low zone local elevators: Local passenger elevators serve the lower zone of the tower. The original 54 local cars are grouped into banks here; placement is schematic.
explanations.mid zone local elevators: Local passenger elevators serve the middle zone of the tower. Placement schematic.
explanations.high zone local elevators: Local passenger elevators serve the upper zone of the tower. Placement schematic.
explanations.freight elevator bank: Eight freight elevators serve the tower. Placement schematic.
explanations.shuttle elevators 80 to 86: Additional elevators connect the 80th floor to the six floors above it.
explanations.shuttle elevators 86 to 102: Elevators run from the 86th floor observatory up through the crown to the 102nd floor.
explanations.observatory service elevator: One elevator connects the 86th and 102nd observatories and the mechanical floors between the 87th and 101st.
explanations.crown lower stage mass: The lower stage of the 16 story, 200 ft (61 m) metal crown above the 86th floor, mostly mechanical.
explanations.crown upper stage mass: The upper stage of the mechanical crown, stepping back below the 102nd floor observatory.
explanations.crown limestone piers: Limestone piers continue the tower rhythm up the crown stages. Detail schematic.
explanations.crown recessed window strips: Recessed window strips light the occupied crown floors between the piers. Detail schematic.
explanations.crown aluminum spandrel bands: Horizontal aluminum spandrel bands cross the crown at each floor line, as on the tower.
explanations.crown mechanical floor core: Mechanical floors fill most of the crown with building systems. Interior shown schematically.
explanations.crown setback ledge: Ledges step the crown back between its two stages and at the roof.
explanations.roof slab, 102nd floor: The roof slab at 1,250 ft (381.0 m), the top of the 102nd floor.
explanations.rooftop penthouses: Rooftop penthouses house elevator overruns and access stairs. Schematic.
explanations.crown parapet: A parapet rings the roof edge at the 102nd floor.
explanations.86th floor deck slab: The deck of the 86th floor observatory at 1,050 ft (320 m), the highest open air observatory.
explanations.86th floor gallery enclosure: An enclosed gallery wraps the 86th floor beside the open air deck.
explanations.86th floor window band: Glazing wraps the enclosed 86th floor gallery.
explanations.86th floor open deck railing: A railing guards the open air deck outside the 86th floor gallery.
explanations.coin operated telescopes: Coin operated telescopes line the 86th floor open deck.
explanations.102nd floor slab: The floor slab of the 102nd floor observatory inside the crown top.
explanations.fully enclosed 102nd floor observatory: The 102nd floor observatory, redesigned in 2019 as a fully enclosed space.
explanations.102nd floor to ceiling glazing: Floor to ceiling windows added in the 2019 redesign ring the 102nd floor observatory.
explanations.indoor 80th floor observatory: The indoor 80th floor observatory, opened in 2019, sits inside the tower.
explanations.wiltshire skyline mural, 80th floor: A skyline mural by Stephen Wiltshire covers a wall of the 80th floor observatory.
explanations.observatory entrance, 20 west 34th: Visitors enter the observatories at 20 West 34th Street, on the north face of the base.
explanations.observatory queuing hall: A queuing hall inside the base organizes the four million yearly observatory visitors. Layout schematic.
explanations.mooring mast tier one: The first of four rectangular mooring mast tiers above the roof, holding the 103rd floor equipment room.
explanations.mooring mast tier two: The second rectangular tier of the mooring mast, stepping back toward the pinnacle.
explanations.mooring mast tier three: The third rectangular tier of the mooring mast.
explanations.mooring mast tier four: The fourth and smallest rectangular tier of the mooring mast.
explanations.mast collar courses: Collar courses step the mast back between its four tiers.
explanations.cylindrical mast shaft: A cylindrical steel shaft tops the four rectangular mast tiers.
explanations.conical mast pinnacle: A conical pinnacle caps the cylindrical mast shaft below the lightning rod.
explanations.lightning rod finial: A lightning rod reaches the 1,454 ft (443.2 m) tip of the building.
explanations.mooring ring for dirigibles: A docking ring marks where airships would have moored at the 106th floor equivalent; the dirigible plan was abandoned because of high winds. Ring schematic.
explanations.103rd floor equipment room: The 103rd floor, originally the planned docking station, now holds electrical equipment.
explanations.103rd floor exterior balcony: An exterior balcony rings the 103rd floor equipment room.
explanations.mast window band: The mast holds 480 windows, replaced in 2015. Placement shown schematically.
explanations.fm broadcast antenna ring: Separate FM antennae ringing the 103rd floor were built in 1965. Arrangement schematic.
explanations.broadcast antenna array: The 200 ft broadcast tower completed in 1953 carries the pinnacle antenna array. Arrangement schematic.
explanations.mast elevator and utility core: The 158 ft hollow steel mast is fitted with elevators and utilities.
explanations.pinnacle maintenance platform: A maintenance platform rings the cylindrical mast shaft. Schematic.
explanations.white searchlight bank: White searchlights were first used in November 1932 to celebrate the Roosevelt victory.
explanations.freedom lights quartet: Four "Freedom Lights" were added in 1956. Placement schematic.
explanations.72nd floor floodlight ring: Floodlights at the 72nd floor were added in February 1964 for the Worlds Fair. Placement schematic.
explanations.metal halide floodlight ring: 204 metal-halide lights were installed in 1976. A schematic subset rings the crown here.
explanations.led fixture ring: 1,200 LED fixtures installed in 2012 light the crown in nine to over 16 million colors. A schematic subset of 360 fixtures is shown.
explanations.spire accent uplights: Uplights wash the mooring mast tiers at night. Placement schematic.
explanations.mast aviation beacons: Aviation beacons mark the mast for aircraft. Placement schematic.
explanations.entry canopy light strips: Light strips glow under the entrance canopies. Placement schematic.
explanations.tower mass, stage 1: The limestone tower mass for floors 6 through 20, one of seven setback stages. The setback floors are mandated by the 1916 Zoning Resolution; stage widths are schematic.
explanations.north south piers, stage 1: Limestone piers stand proud of the north and south faces for floors 6 through 20, alternating wide and narrow in the Art Deco rhythm.
explanations.east west piers, stage 1: Limestone piers stand proud of the east and west faces for floors 6 through 20, alternating wide and narrow in the Art Deco rhythm.
explanations.recessed window bays, stage 1: Window bays for floors 6 through 20 sit recessed between the piers, with nickel-chrome steel mullions. The building has 6,514 windows in total.
explanations.aluminum spandrel bands, stage 1: Horizontal aluminum spandrels join the windows between floors for floors 6 through 20, avoiding cross-bonding in the masonry.
explanations.setback cornice, stage 1: A stone cornice caps stage 1 at its setback, casting the shadow line that makes the zoning steps read from the street.
